title: Sessions that move between machines

story: Nova is at step 4 of 6 on RH-1234. It has read the code, Sean has answered its question about the filter, and it knows why the card must not show while the table is loading. Then the VM freezes. Five minutes later the workflow declares it dead and claims a fresh VM.

The code is safe, because Nova pushed a checkpoint commit after each good step. But the conversation, everything Nova read and decided and the answer Sean gave, was a file on the dead machine's disk. A new session would start from zero, read everything again, and maybe ask Sean the same question twice.
hook.question: Where does a session's memory live, and how do I continue the same conversation on a different machine?

read.h: A session is a file, and resume reads it
p: Every session writes a transcript: a JSON Lines file, one JSON object per line, with every user message, assistant message and tool result in order. By default it lives in ~/.claude/projects/, in a folder named after the working folder with every character that is not a letter or a digit turned into a dash, so /work/fcp becomes -work-fcp. The file name is the session ID from the result message.

Pass that ID as resume in the next query() and the conversation continues with full context: the files it read, the decisions it made, the answers it got. Two related options are worth knowing. continue: true resumes the most recent session in the folder without an ID, and forkSession: true with resume starts a new branch that begins with a copy of the history. Remember what a session does not keep: files. It stores the conversation, not the working folder, which is why Nova also pushes checkpoint commits.

notes.text: Every result carries the session ID, errors included.
resume loads that transcript and the model continues with everything it knew.

read.h: A store that outlives the machine
p: Resume only works if the transcript file is on this machine. To continue somewhere else, the SDK can mirror every transcript to storage you choose, through a session store: an object you write with two required methods. append(key, entries) is called after each batch of entries has been written to the local file, and load(key) returns all the entries of one session in order, or null for a session it never saw. The key has a projectKey, made from the working folder, a sessionId, and a subpath for transcripts of helper agents.

Two rules from the docs shape every store. First, a batch that fails is retried, up to three attempts in all, and after that the SDK drops it, sends a system message with the subtype mirror_error, and continues, because the local copy is safe. Retries mean the same entries can arrive twice, so a store should skip entries whose uuid it has already saved. Second, the SDK never deletes anything from your store, so how long transcripts are kept is your decision.

notes.text: The uuids already saved, so a retried batch does not create duplicate lines.
Helper transcripts arrive with a subpath such as subagents/agent-a1; they get their own folder.
Entries without a uuid, such as titles, are always appended.
One part file per call. Parts sort by name, and the name starts with the time, so load reads them in order.

read.h: Resume on a machine that has never seen the session
p: With a store attached, resume works differently. Before the claude process even starts, the SDK calls load() on your store, writes the entries into a temporary config folder, and starts claude there. The new machine needs nothing on its disk. If you also give the store listSubkeys(), the SDK brings back the helpers' transcripts too; without it, only the main conversation returns.

Three details decide whether this works in practice. The projectKey comes from the working folder, so every machine must use the same one; the harness always works in /work/fcp. A run resumed from the store deletes its local copy at the end, so from then on the store holds the only copy, and a lost batch is really lost. And two options cannot be combined with a store: persistSession: false, because the mirror is built from the local writes, and file checkpointing.

notes.text: Every batch is mirrored to the store folder, next to the normal local transcript.
On run 2 this is the ID from run 1, and the SDK loads it from the store.
Run 2 pretends to be a new machine: a config folder with no transcripts at all.
A batch the store could not save after its retries shows up here.

deeper.h: Go deeper: real stores and the contract test
p: The SDK repositories ship reference stores you can copy: one for an object store (S3, one part file per append, like ours), one for a key-value store (Redis) and one for a database (Postgres). They are examples, not packages, and each takes a client you configure yourself.

The TypeScript examples also include a conformance suite, a set of tests every store must pass, which you copy into your own tests. And the SDK exports InMemorySessionStore for experiments. Note that it does not skip duplicate uuids, as you will see in the lab: dropping duplicates is the job of a production store.

lab.title: Mirror a session to a folder, resume it as a new machine
needs: For the last step only: your own Anthropic API key
lab.goal: Write a session store, prove its contract with tests and no model, then continue a conversation from a config folder that has never seen it.

guess.q: Your store's append() throws for every batch because the network is down. What happens to the session?

options.why: A store outage does not stop the agent. The local transcript is written first and is safe.

options.text: It continues; each failed batch is retried, then dropped with a mirror_error message.
options.why: Up to three attempts per batch, then a system message with subtype mirror_error, and the work goes on.

options.text: The SDK keeps the batches in memory and sends them later.
options.why: After the last attempt the batch is dropped. That is why a run resumed from the store can lose data if you ignore mirror_error.

lab.build: Turn your tests into a contract you can run against any store. Write test/contract.test.ts with a function contract(name, make) that registers two tests for a store made by make(): an unknown session loads as null, and a batch appended twice is stored once. Run it for your FolderSessionStore and for the SDK's InMemorySessionStore, and explain the one failure you see.
checks: Your four store tests pass with no API key.
The contract passes for FolderSessionStore and fails for InMemorySessionStore on the retried batch (4 entries instead of 2).
With your key, run 1 leaves part files under store/.
With your key, run 2 answers tulip from an empty config folder.
lab.fix: A teammate's store names each part part-<n>.jsonl, where n is a counter that starts at 0 in every process. A run on VM 1 wrote part-0 to part-11. The run moved to VM 2 after a crash and wrote part-0 to part-3 again, into the same folder. Now a resumed session sees Sean's answer before the question it answers. Find why, and change the part names so parts written later on any machine always sort after earlier ones.
explain: What does a session keep across a resume, and what does it not keep?
When exactly does the SDK call append() and load(), and what happens when append() keeps failing?
Why must every machine run the session from the same working folder for a stored session to resume?
lab.done: Your store passes its contract tests, and you can continue a conversation from a machine that never had the transcript.

check.q: Nova's VM dies and the run moves to a fresh VM. What brings back what Nova already knew?

options.text: Resuming the session from the store with the same session ID
options.why: load() runs before the claude process starts, so the new VM continues the same conversation.

options.text: The checkpoint commits on the branch
options.why: Commits bring back the files, not the conversation. Both are needed.

options.text: Starting a new session with the same prompt
options.why: A new session starts from zero: it reads everything again and may ask the same questions.

check.q: Your store sometimes receives the same entries twice. Why, and what should it do?

options.text: A bug in the SDK; report it and ignore the duplicates
options.why: It is expected behaviour. A rejected batch is retried, and part of it may already have landed.

options.text: The model repeated itself; filter by message text
options.why: Text can repeat legitimately. Each entry carries a uuid for exactly this purpose.

options.text: Failed batches are retried, so skip entries whose uuid is already stored
options.why: The docs say to treat uuid as an idempotency key, so a retry never creates duplicate lines.

check.q: The run on VM 1 used /work/fcp as its working folder; the resume on VM 2 runs in /home/agent/fcp. What happens?

options.text: It works, because the session ID is unique
options.why: The store's key also contains the projectKey, which comes from the working folder.

options.text: The store is asked for a different projectKey and finds nothing to resume
options.why: Keep the same working folder on every machine; the harness always uses /work/fcp.

options.text: The SDK fixes the path automatically
options.why: There is no such translation; the key is made from the folder the session runs in.

p: Nova's harness passes a session store that writes to S3 through the broker, because the VM has no AWS credentials: each append is a PUT to a URL the broker signs for this run, and load lists and reads the run's parts in order. Part names start with the wall-clock time, so parts written later on another VM sort after earlier ones, and entries are skipped by uuid. The store implements listSubkeys so helper transcripts resume too.

Every VM uses /work/fcp as its working folder, so the projectKey is the same everywhere. The harness watches for mirror_error and posts once if the store keeps failing, since a resumed run's store copy is its only copy. The bucket's 30-day expiry is the only retention, because the SDK never deletes from a store.

tickets.why: store.ts: the S3 store through broker URLs, the key layout, uuid dedupe and listSubkeys.
The workflow spike kills a session halfway and resumes it, which depends on this lesson.

words.plain: The JSON Lines file of a session: every message and tool result, in order.
The option that loads a session by ID, so the conversation continues with full context.
Your object with append() and load() that mirrors transcripts to storage you choose.
The part of a store key made from the working folder; it must match on every machine.
The system message the SDK sends when a batch could not be saved to the store after its retries.

review.q: Name the two required methods of a session store and when each is called.
review.a: append(key, entries) after each batch is written locally; load(key) once, before the claude process starts, when you resume.

review.q: Why do Nova's part names start with the time and not a counter?
review.a: A counter restarts on each new VM, so later parts could sort before earlier ones. Wall-clock time keeps the order across machines.

remember: A session is a transcript; mirror it with a store, keep the working folder the same, and any machine can resume it.
